# Design ## Approach Add an optional `limit` keyword to `Table.search`, validating that it is a non‑negative integer. The method will continue to use the existing query‑cache for the full result set, then apply the limit when returning a copy to the caller. This preserves current behaviour when `limit` is omitted and works for both the default and named tables because all table objects share the same `search` implementation. No other modules need changes. ## Changes | File | Function or class | Change | ACs | |---|---|---|---| | tinydb/table.py | Table.search | • Change signature to `def search(self, cond: QueryLike, limit: int | None = None) -> list[Document]`.
• Add validation: if `limit` is not `None` and not an `int` or is negative, raise `ValueError('limit must be a non‑negative integer')`.
• After obtaining `docs` (the full matching list) and before caching, store the full list in the cache as before.
• Return `docs[:limit]` when `limit` is provided, otherwise return a full copy (`docs[:]`). This keeps the cache unchanged and satisfies ordering. | AC‑1, AC‑2, AC‑3, AC‑4 | | tinydb/__init__.py | (none) | No changes required; the public API forwards to `Table.search`, which now accepts `limit`. | – | | tinydb/tests (if any) | (none) | No test files need modification; existing tests will continue to pass, and new tests for the limit behaviour can be added without altering current ones. | – | ## Existing tests affected none ## Risks - Introducing a `ValueError` for invalid limits may surface in user code that previously passed non‑integer values; however, this aligns with the assumption A‑1 that limits must be non‑negative integers. - Slicing after caching ensures the cache stores the full result set; if a future change relies on the cached list being exactly what was returned, it could be impacted, but current TinyDB usage only reads from the cache internally.
